items.title: Tom Baker interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 13, 1997
items.q: I really like the cool school — the Art Pepper, Paul Desmond, Gerry Mulligan stuff

ctx.x: What’s the most contemporary — oh I don’t want to use that word, let me use a different word — what’s the most modern, chronologically, type of jazz you would care to play?

Gee. Probably Charlie Parker style bebop. That era. Forties bebop. And also I really like the cool school — the Art Pepper, Paul Desmond, Gerry Mulligan stuff — maybe being a west coast boy, I’ve really got an affinity for that. But I really like that. But the hard bop stuff I can’t understand and certainly the modal thing from the 60s and all that free stuff, I can’t say I don’t like it, but I can’t do it. I’ve tried, but I can’t do it.
Can you think of the weirdest, toughest gig that you’ve ever played?
